question.problem:
The data sets $x$ and $y$ have the following properties:

$$
{S}_{xx}=41,\,{S}_{xy}=-39,\,{S}_{yy}=61
$$

Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall the definitions of ${S}_{xx},$ ${S}_{xy},$ and ${S}_{yy}$ for the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}:$

$$
{S}_{xx}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2},\,{S}_{xy}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),\,{S}_{yy}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2}
$$

The linear correlation coefficient $\rho $ of the data sets $x$ and $y$ is given by 

$$
\rho (x,y)=\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}}=\frac{{S}_{xy}}{\sqrt{{S}_{xx}\cdot {S}_{yy}}}.
$$

Using the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{(-39)}{\sqrt{41}\cdot \sqrt{61}} \\  & ≈-\frac{39}{6.403\,124\cdot 7.810\,250} \\  & ≈-0.78\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
